title: NVIDIA now automatically enables AI server in NVIDIA App, here’s how to disable it
source_used: Tbreak (relaying VideoCardz) and IGN; VideoCardz page was blocked
key_facts: Nvidia added an option for AI agents to control the Nvidia App in version 11.0.9.565 on 13 Oct 2026 (IGN).

Patch notes: the app includes a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets a compatible AI agent control the app with natural-language requests, for example applying optimal settings or enabling ShadowPlay recording.
VideoCardz found the feature already switched on after updating, and reports other users saw the same (Tbreak); IGN says it is on by default and not exclusive to RTX Spark systems.
Users including Silent Hill: Ascension cinematic director Agustin Cordes warned of a security risk; one user who appears to be a cybersecurity professional said there are no reported exploits yet.
The server runs locally at 127.0.0.1, port 13508 by default; an agent using a cloud service could send retrieved information to that service (Tbreak, citing VideoCardz).
To disable: Nvidia App, Settings, 'AI Agents and App Connections' (Features, Connect Agents & Apps), switch off 'Allow Agents to control Nvidia App'.
IGN reached out to Nvidia about the security implications and will update; Nvidia's release notes confirm MCP support but do not explain the default-on behaviour (Tbreak).
quote_evidence: Nvidia added the option in Nvidia App 11.0.9.565 on October 13.
The problem really seems to be that the Nvidia App update turns the setting on by default, which is almost a surefire way to get people to hate any given feature in a tech product.
The automatic activation is VideoCardz’s observation, supported by other user reports it cites.
why_it_matters_hint: An update quietly opens a path for AI agents to control a widely installed PC app, which some users see as a security risk.
event_date: Update 13 Oct 2026; default-on finding and warnings 16 Oct 2026
notes: VideoCardz original blocked; its findings read via Tbreak. IGN is first-hand on the patch notes and user reactions.
